passages.provision_quote: shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose any information related to a pupil’s sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression to any other person without the pupil’s consent, unless otherwise required by state or federal law.
passages.note: Chaptered text (the text voted on at Assembly concurrence): Sec. 220.5 forbids local policies requiring disclosure without consent; it does not require staff to withhold, so the rung-1 mandate is not met, and it bars disclosure-on-request rules.
Aye on Assembly concurrence in Senate amendments (final passage of the chaptered text), 61-16, about 21% No, so not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Schiavo voted Aye on final Assembly passage of AB 1955 (2023-2024), whose operative Sec. 220.5 says local educational agencies "shall not enact or enforce any policy, rule, or administrative regulation that would require an employee or a contractor to disclose" a pupil's gender identity without consent. That matches the rung "Forbid rules that require schools to tell parents"; the bill does not require staff to keep the information from parents, so the rung requiring secrecy is not met.
